newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks end up strong, despite US holiday.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks end up strong, despite US holiday.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up in brisk trade, despite the US memorial day holiday, on the expectation of tariff increases for market bellwether Electricidad de Caracas, traders said.
"There are rumors of a new Electricidad dividend and also tariff increases," said Econoinvest broker Gabriel Osio.

But a high ranking company official said the rumor was, "just that, a rumor. As for the tariff hike, well we're still waiting." Electricidad, which is in near constant battle with the Energy and Mines Ministry over tariff increases, paid a one-for-25 stock dividend last week.
The bolsa's 19-share index gained 1.20 percent to end at 6,827.50 points as among traded issues 26 rose, six fell and seven closed flat.

Trade was boosted to 189 million shares, worth seven billion bolivars ($4.3 million), by large cross trades in paints and packaging company Corimon B shares, which accounted for nearly two thirds of the day's volume.
"It was a strong market, with much demand but rather illiquid ... there were few sellers, perhaps because of the US holiday," said Activalores broker Carlos Sanchez.
Merinvest's composite index, which includes telephone company CANTV, rose 1.2 percent to close at 108.46 points.
